title: The great circle: the Kav's first will, like a man's taste and his dream house
overview:
The *Kav* goes down in circles (*igulim*) and in a straight line (*yosher*) shaped like a person, and its first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, surrounds all four worlds equally. To explain it the chapter sets out two kinds of will. The simple will in the Essence is like a person's taste or style: it shapes how he will do every kindness and think every thought, yet it is hidden, part of his self-knowledge, with no general and particular. Only when he comes to build does it become a composite will: one general picture of the house, then the kitchen, the sink, down to the *mezuza* on the door.

Above, *tehiru ila'a* is G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way. After the *tzimtzum* comes the choice: this world, all the way to *Moshiach*, as one *ratzon kadum* that includes every detail, even each hair and each leaf in the wind. Everything after it, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, down to the weather today, is only a means to that goal. That a will can be cut off from its goal is the root of *Tohu*.

terms.gloss: circles: the ten concentric circles the Kav makes as it goes down, like the soul before it comes into the body
the straight line: the sefiros in the form of a person, three lines, like the soul in the body with each power in its own kli
the lower purity: the first circle after the hiyuli Kav, the ultimate goal; self-knowledge of how something separate relates to Him
the raw potential from which all the particular drawings-down branch off
the simple will in the Essence, still one with it; it cannot yet be called a general thought
the absolute will: like a person's taste or style, which shapes every choice and stays hidden
the composite will: a will for something in the world, with a general thing, details and priorities
self-knowledge: knowing what you will want because you know yourself
the upper purity: before the tzimtzum, only G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way
the original will: the ultimate goal, of which everything after it is only a detail and a means
the encompassing light; the first circle surrounds all four worlds equally

sections.title: Circles and the straight line: the first circle is tehiru tata'a
sections.summary: The chapter now explains the *makifim* and *pnimiyim* in the *Kav*: the ten circles (*igulim*) it makes as it goes down, and the straight line (*yosher*) in the form of a person. The first circle, right after the *hiyuli Kav*, is *tehiru tata'a*, the general *makif* over all four worlds equally: the ultimate goal of the whole chain.

phrases.he: (טז) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין הקו וחוט זה, איך שיש בו בחינת מקיפים ופנימיים
phrases.en: Now we're going to explain the *inyan* of *igulim v'yosher*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים מתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו' (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.text:
Chapter 16 is "a nice *perek*": short, quick and simple, one *inyan* that most people find *geshmak* (tasty); "it sits very well."

**Now we're going to explain the inyan of igulim v'yosher**: the circles (*igulim*) and the straight line (*yosher*), the *makifim* and *pnimiyim* of the *Kav*.

As *Etz Chaim* says, it "circles and returns and circles." The *hiyuli Kav* goes down a little and makes a circle, goes down more and makes another, until there are ten: the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* of *Adam Kadmon*. Then comes *yosher*.

Really *igulim* and *yosher* are two separate *hishtalshelus*'s (chains of descent): every world has ten *sefiros* of *igulim* and ten of *yosher*.

blocks.question: Is it like a spring?
blocks.text: No. Picture concentric circles with a line going through them. It does not spiral: each circle is full and closes, then from the same line it goes down and makes the next. A *Kav* comes from one side, going down and making all the circles.

blocks.title: Water filling carved troughs
blocks.text:
From the side of the *reshimu* the circles are set up from below to above and are not connected at all. When *yosher* comes down, the *Kav* starts from the top, and in the light they are connected.

It is as if troughs were engraved in the shape of circles and water came down from the top: it hits the first trough, fills it, overflows to the next and goes around that one. What makes the light stop and circle in each place? The *reshimu* has already carved out an *igul* there. And it does not fill the inside; it only goes around the rim, so to speak. "You could make like a bead thing, like with a marble." That line is the *yosher* of the *igulim*.

These are the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* as they are in the light. After them comes *yosher*, a parallel *hishtalshelus* on top of it: the *sefiros* of *yosher* in the shape of a person, the three lines of *Chabad*, *Chagas*, *Nehi*, *chachma* on the right and *bina* on the left. "That whole *tzura* of an *adam* is the *yosher*."

The two chains overlap. The *igulim* start a little higher; from about their *bina* it connects right to *yosher*, and the rest of the *igulim* are in the same place as *yosher*.

blocks.title: The soul before and in the body
blocks.text:
The *igulim* are like the soul before it comes into the body; *yosher* is the soul in the body, where each part gets its own *kli* (vessel) and becomes a *partzuf*. In the soul all the powers are as one: the power of will and the power of walking are the same thing, because when it wants something it is already drawn to it. It is all spiritual, so all ten happen together. In the body each power is distinct, tied to its own *kli*, and that lets you appreciate each one.

The *mashal* in this chapter and the next three will make clear what *igulim* and *yosher* mean.

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף ועיגול הראשון
phrases.en: in the first circle, right after the *hiyuli Kav*, there's the first circle.

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה כו',
phrases.en: That's called the lower purity.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת המקיף הכללי שמקיף לד' עולמות דאבי''ע בשווה
phrases.en: This is the general *makif* that surrounds the four worlds of *ABYA* equally.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text:
**In the first circle, right after the hiyuli Kav, there's the first circle**: **that's called the lower purity**, *tehiru tata'a*, the first *gilui* (revelation) of the will for the *hishtalshelus* after the *tzimtzum*: the general *makif*, *sovev kol almin*, the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.

Before it is the *reshis hakav* (beginning of the line), the *kav hamida* (line of measure), only a *hiyuli* for the particular revelations.

blocks.title: The teacher's ultimate goal
blocks.text: Once the teacher has figured out his system, how to divide up the subject into levels to measure the student, he makes his first circle: the ultimate goal of this will, of this whole *hishtalshelus*.

blocks.title: Rabbi Chodakov and the shliach to South Africa
blocks.text:
This is the unrealistic goal of the Rabbi Chodakov story from the *farbrengen*. A *shliach* (emissary) was going to South Africa, and Rabbi Chodakov asked him, "Do you have a plan for what you're planning to do there?" He said, "No, when I get there, I'll see."

The point: your goal first has to be your pure, unrealistic goal. "What do you want essentially? Then you figure out how to make it fit in."

So this first circle is what the teacher figures out first: "What would be the ultimate thing for the students to come out from this class with?" It is the all-encompassing desire that includes any scenario in this classroom, in this *hishtalshelus*, because it is the best you could get within it.

**This is the general makif that surrounds the four worlds of ABYA equally**, what is usually called *sovev kol almin*. The light before the *tzimtzum* is sometimes also called *sovev kol almin*, but that is different: it is not a *sovev* on a *pnimi*, as will be explained. **Like it says in Etz Chaim.**

sections.title: The Kav as one general thought that sees to the end
sections.summary: First the *Kav* as a whole: one *hiyuli* from which all the particular drawings-down branch off. It is like a general thought that sees to the end of all generations at a glance, as a man who wants a house already wants the kitchen, the sink and the running water.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים
phrases.en: but first we have to explain,

phrases.he: כללות ענין הקו הזה, איך שהוא בחינת היולי כללי לכל הסתעפות המשכות פרטיים הרבה שמסתעפים ממנו עד סוף העשיה כו' כנזכר לעיל
ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע בענין מחשבה כללית
שבמחשבה זו הכללית צופה ומביט עד סוף כל הדורות בסקירה א'
phrases.en: that with this general thought Hashem sees the whole *hishtalshelus*, with the whole history of mankind, all the way to the end,

phrases.he: (ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו מה שבידיעת עצמו יודע את כל הנבראים
phrases.en: This is what the *Rambam* describes, that by knowing Himself He knows all the *nivra'im*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: **But first we have to explain** the *Kav* as a whole: how it is one general *hiyuli* for all the many particular drawings-down that branch off from it, down to the end of *Asiya*. *Mistaef* means to branch off, "whatever *lashon* it is."

It is understood from the known *mashal* of a general thought: **with this general thought Hashem sees the whole hishtalshelus**, the whole history of mankind, to the end of the seventh millennium, the total completion, past *Moshiach* (the end of the sixth). This is called the *ratzon kadum* or *machshava kduma*.

In the Rambam's words: **by knowing Himself He knows all the nivra'im** (the created beings).

blocks.title: Do you want a sink in your kitchen?
blocks.text:
How can one thought include everything? Take a guy who wants a house. "Do you want a kitchen in your house?" "What do you mean? Of course. What kind of a house would it be without a kitchen?" "Do you want a sink in your kitchen?" "What kind of a kitchen would it be without the sink?" "Okay, so you want a sink. Do you want running water in your sink?"

You could go through the whole house like this. The word "house" is one thought that includes all the details, even less obvious ones, because he wants *his* house: since he knows himself, what he likes, he knows what he wants in it.

blocks.title: 126,282 hairs on his head
blocks.text: So if G-d said He wants a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), you ask Him, "Do you want this and this guy in it?" "What do you mean? How can I have a *dira b'tachtonim* without this guy?" Even "Do you want him to have 126,282 hairs on his head?" "He wouldn't be Moishe without that." All the details are included like this.

sections.title: Two kinds of will: the simple will is a person's taste, the composite will has priorities
sections.summary: The simple will in the Essence is like a person's taste or style: it already shapes how he will do every kindness and think every thought, but it is hidden and has no general and particular. Only when it comes to action does it become a composite will (*ratzon murkav*): a general thought with particulars under it, circle within circle.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע
שיש ב' מיני רצון
phrases.en: There's two types of desires.

phrases.he: א' רצון הפשוט שבעצמות
phrases.en: One is the simple *ratzon* that's in the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: שנכלל בעצמותו ממש,
שלא נקרא עדיין בשם בחינת מחשבה ורצון כללי
phrases.en: You can't call it a general thought or general *ratzon* yet,

phrases.he: כי מתאחד עדיין בעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: still one with his *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: כמו גם שהוחלט רצון זה כבר בעצמו
phrases.en: even the way that he has already predetermined in himself, so to speak,

phrases.he: איך לעשות דבר חסד פלוני
או איך לדבר ולחשוב אותו
phrases.en: or what he's going to say, and what he's going to think.

phrases.he: או להשכיל שכל פרטי
phrases.en: or also the way that each person understands things in different ways.

phrases.he: או להיות לו רצון ותענוג בדבר כו'
phrases.en: or whether he's going to enjoy something or not enjoy something,

blocks.text: **There's two types of desires.** **One is the simple ratzon that's in the Atzmus**, the *ratzon hapashut*, included in His very essence. **You can't call it a general thought or general ratzon yet**, because it is **still one with his Atzmus**.

It includes **even the way that he has already predetermined in himself, so to speak**, how to do a particular kindness: his taste. The *ratzon hamuchlat* (absolute will) is his taste or style, already in his essence. It is not a desire or thought about the outside world but part of his self-knowledge, a sense of who he is and how he wants to express himself: a certain estimation, made like *Kadmon*, of how he wants to reveal himself.

So he already knows that if such a situation comes up he will want to give the guy the coat, and he will. Each person has his way; if you know a person really well, you can predict how he will do something. This is the level of *Kadmon* spoken of before: the *ratzon hamuchlat* is *Kadmon*.

From *Kadmon* a little of it actually comes out, but not *b'pnimiyus* (inwardly), as will be explained, because a person's taste is not yet a desire for any particular thing; it relates to everything he does: how he wants to do it, **or what he's going to say, and what he's going to think**. Even his thinking includes his biases: when a situation comes up, different people think about it in their own way.

**Or also the way that each person understands things in different ways**: as will be said later, Rashi, Tosafos, everybody has his own *shita* (approach), a way of understanding that is unique. **Or whether he's going to enjoy something or not**, what he will like and what he will hate: "all these things are included in his taste basically."

phrases.he: הגם שמתחבר רצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון בדבר הפרטי
phrases.en: even though this taste connects to the actual desire, it influences it,

phrases.he: אבל נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמותו
phrases.en: but it stays really hidden.

phrases.he: ועל כן אין בו עדיין בחינת כלל ופרט כו'
phrases.en: and that therefore their taste does not have a *klal u'prat*.

blocks.text: **Even though this taste connects to the actual desire, it influences it, but it stays really hidden.**

blocks.title: The artist's style
blocks.text: Take an artist with a certain style. The style is nothing tangible. His painting is influenced by his style, but you cannot say the painting is his style, and you cannot copy it or say what it is. Sometimes people try to figure out their style and do those things, "and it comes out fake."

A style means you are just being yourself, naturally. Books on writing, or on any art, put it nicely: "the style is the person himself." *Davka* (precisely) when you let yourself come out freely, without putting anything on, not even acting the way you see yourself, it comes out in everything you do. Yet it is nothing you can point to: a painting can be impressionistic, but you cannot say it is impressionism.

The same way, a person's taste influences every desire he ever has, but no desire is a direct expression of his full taste.

**And that therefore their taste does not have a klal u'prat** (general and particular). When a person wants a house, the main thing is the building with a roof, protection from the elements. Secondary are the furniture and utilities; then decorating, paint, carpeting or a wood floor, and then the bathroom drapes.

It is all influenced by his taste. But in an actual will there is a main thing: the first, main circle is for a house, a general picture of what a house means. Within it is a circle for the kitchen, for the living room, dining room, bedroom and bathroom, each included in the circle of the house; and each of those has circles in it, like the sink and the stove in the kitchen, smaller and smaller, down to the bathroom drapes.

But the taste influences each stage equally. Whenever there is a choice of how to do it, big or small, that choice comes from his taste, his *ratzon hamuchlat*, so each is an expression of it just like anything else.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זה עולה רצון זה שהוחלט אצלו לבוא לידי מעשה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: but when this *ratzon* is going to come now *b'poel mamash*,

phrases.he: הרי יוצא מהעלמו לגלוי
phrases.en: when it comes *b'poel mamash*, actually do it, then it becomes revealed, *l'gilui*,

phrases.he: אז יבוא הרצון בבחינת כלל ופרט,
phrases.en: then there's a general thing and there's the particulars,

phrases.he: דהיינו מחשבה כללית
phrases.en: first there's the general thought

phrases.he: שכוללת כל ענין המעשה מראש לסוף בסקירה א'
phrases.en: that includes everything at once,

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצונות פרטיים
phrases.en: then it divides to particular desires,

phrases.he: ולכל רצון שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and each one has its own *sechel* and *middos* and everything,

phrases.he: ובאין זה אחר זה בהשתלשלות
phrases.en: and they come one after the other,

phrases.he: זה עליון מקיף לתחתון,
phrases.en: the upper one encompassing the lower one,

phrases.he: כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך האופן כו'
phrases.en: like a circle inside of a circle, concentric circles.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא רצון המורכב שיש בו כלל ופרט
phrases.en: that's called a *ratzon murkav*, a complex *ratzon*.

blocks.text: **But when this ratzon is going to come now b'poel mamash** (into actual deed): if you know someone well, you could figure out his dream house before he ever thought of buying one; but there you cannot speak of general and particular, because there is no deed at all. He did not even think about it.

And what you recognize is how his taste would come out in the society we are in now. The same person in a different time would express the same taste differently: instead of a nice, big mansion, he would want a hut if he were a tribal chief in Africa.

sensitivity.reason: Illustrates another time and place with "a hut if he were a tribal chief in Africa"; not meant as disparaging, but a stereotype of Africa a public edition may prefer to drop.
sensitivity.publishable: And what you recognize is how his taste would come out in the society we are in now. The same person in a different time would express the same taste differently: instead of a nice, big mansion, he would want whatever house fit a leader of that time and place.

blocks.text: **When it comes b'poel mamash, actually do it, then it becomes revealed**, and **then there's a general thing and there's the particulars**: priorities. **First there's the general thought that includes everything at once**, defining the general goal. **Then it divides to particular desires, and each one has its own sechel and middos** (intellect and emotions), **and they come one after the other**, **the upper one encompassing the lower one**: it defines and includes the lower, which is a detail serving its purpose, **like a circle inside of a circle, concentric circles.**

A general will for the house, a particular will for the kitchen, and within that the wills for the sink and the rest: **that's called a ratzon murkav, a complex ratzon**. *Murkav* means composite, made of many parts. The taste is a simple will, *ratzon pashut*; when you actually want something in the world it is complex: the general thing has details, each with sub-details, so there is already a *klal* and a *prat*.

*Murkav* also means there are priorities. A simple thing from the essence is just a *nekuda* (a point). Here it is complicated: you can have conflicting desires, you want this and you want that, you want this because it will do that, "it's like a whole bubble already." The choice in each will comes from the *ratzon pashut*, from his *ratzon hamuchlat*.

But the actual picture, the way it comes out physically, is *murkav*. As will be said soon, maybe at the start of the next chapter, the *ratzon hamuchlat* is really for himself, a self-expression: he is comfortable *davka* in a certain way, he wants a certain atmosphere, and the house he wants expresses him. As far as that goes, the *ratzon hamuchlat* is just a will to express himself.

sections.title: The mashal: a man who wants to build a great building
sections.summary: The taste a man already has for a building is still within himself, as if it did not exist; the house is not yet wanted. When he comes to build, the details he had already settled appear, first as one general picture, then will after will down to the last screw and the *mezuza* on the door.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע,
אדם שרוצה לבנות בנין גדול
phrases.en: a person wants to build a big building,

phrases.he: כפי הרצון שהוחלת מכבר אצלו
phrases.en: according to his taste,

phrases.he: להיות בו אופנים מיוחדים דוקא
phrases.en: he wants it to be specially designed for the way he wants it.

phrases.he: שאותו הרצון שהוחלט אצלו מכבר,
phrases.en: that this taste that he had already decided before,

phrases.he: הגם שהוא בא במדה ותענוג מיוחד
phrases.en: even though in a way it is like defined, that each person has a certain thing, they enjoy things in a certain way,

phrases.he: באופן כך וכך,
וממילא בשכל ומדות בא בשיעור ומדה כו',
phrases.en: and since he enjoys things a certain way, that automatically influences that his *sechel* leans to try to find that; everything is in line with that.

phrases.he: אך כל זה הוא השיעור וההחלט שבעצמותו עדיין,
phrases.en: that's all still within his essence,

phrases.he: ונכלל בעצמו
phrases.en: and it's really part of himself,

phrases.he: והיה כלא היה כו'
phrases.en: it's like it doesn't exist; he doesn't actually have a desire yet for a house.

blocks.text: From a known *mashal*: **a person wants to build a big building, according to his taste**; **he wants it to be specially designed for the way he wants it**: a dream house, or a dream facility for his Chabad house, "doesn't make a difference what it is."

**This taste that he had already decided before**, **even though in a way it is like defined**, since each person enjoys things in a certain way, which **automatically influences that his sechel leans to try to find that**: **that's all still within his essence**, **really part of himself**: **it's like it doesn't exist; he doesn't actually have a desire yet for a house.**

If you know him, you know how he would want it, but he has no desire for it yet, no thought of anything outside himself: it is *yedias atzmo* (self-knowledge). How do you know what you want in a house? You think what makes you happy; you know how you want to feel. That is its *pnimiyus* (inner side): the way you want to feel, and liking to do things a certain way.

It comes because he set up in his personality *b'kadmonius* a certain *teva* (nature), so to speak, for himself: the form he chose to express himself with, which comes out in the world according to whatever situation it meets.

That is the *inyan* of *teshuva*: you reconnect the external desires to their source, and the farther up you go, the more "it's like hitting the reset button." The higher you change a desire, the more flexible everything under it becomes. At the essence everything is flexible, because the inner desire there is to express that you have *bechira* (free choice), that your *etzem* is above any thing, not stuck in any.

That is the usual order of *avoda*. First a person takes his nature, the way he is, and uses it for good. The next step is to break out of his nature: not *iskafya* (forcing himself against it), but freeing himself, realizing that the personality he thinks is him "is really just like a role that they're acting out," a costume, and he can choose to act out a different role.

You see it by Avraham having to do *gevura*, and Yaakov, an *ish tam* (a simple, wholesome man), having "to lie and cheat" Esav and Lavan: they had to do the opposite of their nature. ("Not sure what it was by Yitzchak really.") *Davka* when a person does this, he reveals his *etzem*.

sensitivity.reason: Says Yaakov Avinu had "to lie and cheat" Esav and Lavan; the point is a Torah one, but the blunt wording about a patriarch may need his approval in print.
sensitivity.publishable: You see it by Avraham having to do *gevura*, and Yaakov, an *ish tam* (a simple, wholesome man), having to deal deceptively with Esav and Lavan: they had to do the opposite of their nature. ("Not sure what it was by Yitzchak really.") *Davka* when a person does this, he reveals his *etzem*.

blocks.title: The Purim costume
blocks.text: On Purim, in a costume, you feel free to do what you want, because it does not reflect on you. Similarly, from the side of the *yechida* a person realizes that all the *partzufim* he puts on, all the roles he plays, are costumes he can take off.

You see it in the Rebbe, who was very unpredictable: with each person and in each situation he acted differently, at every extreme, the most private and the most public, the most liberal and the most conservative. Normally these look like contradictions. "The whole thing really of Chassidus, when you reveal the essence, is that you realize you can have 100% of both": in a conflict it is not 50-50, or all of one.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זמן באה מחשבה זו לבא למעשה,
phrases.en: but when later he actually thinks, "Oh, I want to build a house,"

phrases.he: ניכר בו התחלקות אותן אופנים שונים ממש שכבר הוחלט אצלו בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: Now then you see everything that was already decided there with all the details.

phrases.he: רק שמתחלה בא הרצון הזה בדרך כלל
phrases.en: first comes as a general thought,

phrases.he: שיהיה לו בנין בציור כך וכך
phrases.en: he wants this general type of a house,

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצון פרטי
phrases.en: and then he plans out where he wants the house to be, how he's gonna pay for it, exactly how he's gonna decorate it, all the details he thinks of later.

phrases.he: לכל ענין פרטי
phrases.en: for each detail, like the kitchen, and the sink, and whatever.

phrases.he: ויורד ובא בסדר והדרגה מכלל הראשון
phrases.en: from the first general *klal*, like the *ratzon* for a house,

phrases.he: שכולל הכל בסקירה א'
לפרט רצון שהוא נקרא כלל לגבי רצונות המסתעפים ממנו
phrases.en: Then he goes from the general *ratzon* of a house to a detail of that, like the kitchen, but that's then a general thing for everything that branches off from it,

phrases.he: עד שבא אל רצון ושכל פרטי היותר אחרון
phrases.en: until it comes to the last screw,

phrases.he: שבסוף מעשה בכלות הכל כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: putting up the *mezuza* on his front door when he's finished everything.

blocks.text: **But when later he actually thinks, "Oh, I want to build a house,"** not just that he already had in him the way he would want to do it, but he actually thought about it: **now then you see everything that was already decided there with all the details.**

blocks.title: Advertising
blocks.text:
By the way, the same idea on a little lower level is advertising. It is not trying to find someone who right now wants a car. It wants him to set up, subconsciously, a positive association with the name, so that one day, when he goes to buy, he thinks of your name right away, or, faced with two names, picks yours. He was not thinking of buying, but he associated it with something that fits his personality: being free, being put together. They give the product an image, so that people who want to express themselves through that image will choose it.

The real *ratzon hamuchlat* here is the image a person wants to express himself as. Advertisers do not set it; "they're just trying to tap into that."

All that was settled in his *ratzon hamuchlat* now comes out *l'poel* (into action), as he actually wants to build a house in this world. It **first comes as a general thought**: **he wants this general type of a house**. **And then he plans out where he wants the house to be, how he's gonna pay for it, exactly how he's gonna decorate it**, **for each detail, like the kitchen, and the sink**.

It goes down by levels, **from the first general klal, like the ratzon for a house**, which includes everything at one glance, to a detail like the kitchen, **but that's then a general thing for everything that branches off from it**, **until it comes to the last screw**: **putting up the mezuza on his front door when he's finished everything.**

That is the idea of the ten *sefiros* of *igulim*. The first circle is the general will for the whole *dira b'tachtonim*. Then, as the *nimshal* will say, it splits into the will for *Atzilus* and for *Beriya*, each into the ten *sefiros* of its world, down to each *prat*, "even like for each person and each little creature that Hashem made."

sections.title: The nimshal above: tehiru ila'a is the taste still within the Essence
sections.summary: Before the *tzimtzum*, in *tehiru ila'a*, G-d has the knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way, like the taste in the simple will: not yet a will for anything outside Himself, so it cannot even be called a general thought. *Tehiru tata'a*, after the *tzimtzum*, is the choice of this world: still self-knowledge, but of how something separate relates to Him, so a lower purity.

phrases.he: והנמשל מכל זה יובן למעלה בהפרש שבין בחינת טהירו עילאה ובין בחינת טהירו תתאה שלאחר הצמצום

blocks.text: The *nimshal* of all this is understood above, in the difference between *tehiru ila'a* and *tehiru tata'a* after the *tzimtzum*. *Tehiru ila'a* is like the essential simple will and what comes out from it, *Yachid* and *Kadmon*; the part of it that relates to *tehiru tata'a* is *Kadmon*. *Tehiru tata'a*, after the *tzimtzum*, is the actual revealed will.

Before the *tzimtzum* is the *etzem*, and included in it, like a *hiyuli*, is G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself any way He wants, our world included: if He ever chose to, He would know how, and could. The *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* were to pick which way He would reveal Himself. The first *ratzon kadum*, the result of *tzimtzum*, *reshimu* and *Kav*, is that choice, starting off as the general thought of our world.

That is the product: G-d thought of our world, the whole totality of it, that He will reveal Himself as Creator of man, with *galus* (exile), *geula* (redemption) and *dira b'tachtonim*. Revealing the *etzem* is not in this *ratzon kadum*, "I don't think," because that is higher. But the whole *Moshiach* thing is the first *ratzon kadum*: one particular way G-d could reveal Himself, through this whole *hishtalshelus*. That is *tehiru tata'a*.

phrases.he: דמה ששיער בעצמו בכח בטהירו עילאה כו'
phrases.en: that in *tehiru ila'a* it's just that Hashem has in His ability the knowledge of how to do it and the ability to do it.

phrases.he: הוא כמו ההחלט ברצון הפשוט שבעצמות הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like a taste,

phrases.he: שעדיין לא בא כלל לבחינת התפשטות חוץ מן העצמות עדיין
phrases.en: It's not at all an actual *ratzon* for something separate from Himself.

phrases.he: וגם שיתחבר מרצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון שאחר כך,
phrases.en: even though this connects to the *hispashtus* of the *ratzon*

phrases.he: מכל מקום נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: The *ratzon muchlat* stays really hidden.

phrases.he: ועל כן למעלה הוא מבחינת כלל להיות נקרא צופה ומביט בסקירה א' כו'.
phrases.en: Therefore, at that stage you can't even call it a general thing, a general thought of our world that's in a *skira achas*.

blocks.text: What He estimated in Himself *b'koach* (in potential) means **that in tehiru ila'a it's just that Hashem has in His ability the knowledge of how to do it and the ability to do it**, **like a taste**. **It's not at all an actual ratzon for something separate from Himself.** **Even though this connects to the hispashtus of the ratzon**, **the ratzon muchlat stays really hidden**: not being a *makif* and *pnimi*, it never becomes revealed, not even the *hashara* (estimation) of *Kadmon*, which before the *tzimtzum* includes knowing how to make any *hishtalshelus*.

**Therefore, at that stage you can't even call it a general thing, a general thought of our world that's in a skira achas** (one glance): it is not yet a thought of something outside, only *yedias atzmo*. That is why *tehiru ila'a* is completely pure.

*Tehiru tata'a* is G-d looking at the world as an expression of Himself: still *yedias atzmo*, but one with a *nivra* (a created being) in it. So it is a lower purity: a self-revelation of how something separate relates to you.

So you are still thinking of yourself. As will be said, the *ratzon kadum* is not yet a will for a house; "it's a ratzon for a home": the feeling you will get from it. Picturing an actual physical house according to your society happens in *Adam Kadmon*, as will be explained.

blocks.title: The clingy baby
blocks.text: At a certain age a person wants to be independent, to settle down; that is in human nature: "a person without a house is not a person." In the *ratzon hamuchlat* you know it even of a clingy baby who will not let go of his mother for a second: "I'm telling you, one day he's going to want to get out of here and have his own house and only come back and visit every now and then." "How do you know?" "I know the nature of people." The kid does not know it, and would not believe you.

At first it is not a will to buy an apartment or a house but an uneasiness: he feels unsettled and looks for what will fit. Then he visits somebody with his own place, feels the independence it gives, and realizes the uneasy feeling was a will for that.

So the *ratzon kadum* is already a will for a particular *taanug* (delight) to be fulfilled in the outside world, to express yourself there in a certain way; you are only looking for what will do it. That is why the *igulim* are like the soul: not yet enclothed in the tangible world.

sections.title: The second will: the Kav and its first circle, the ratzon kadum
sections.summary: After the *tzimtzum*, the simple will comes to spread forth: that is the *hiyuli Kav*, a general system of priorities. Its first product is the ultimate goal, the first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, which includes every particular will and is called *ratzon kadum*: everything after it is only a means to it.

phrases.he: אך הרצון הב' הוא אחר הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
שעולה רצון הפשוט המוחלט שבעצמות לבא לידי בחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: that something from this *ratzon pashut* came to actually do it, that Hashem decided, picked what He's going to actually do.

phrases.he: הוא בחינת הקו וחוט ההיולי שכולל כל המשכות פרטיות שבו מראשו לסופו כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: The second will is after the *tzimtzum*: the simple, absolute will in the Essence rises to spread forth, meaning **that something from this ratzon pashut came to actually do it, that Hashem decided, picked what He's going to actually do.** That is the *hiyuli Kav*, which includes all the particular drawings-down from its beginning to its end.

This is the general *inyan* of the *Kav*. The *reshimu*, with the head of the *Kav*, is the general goal; the *Kav* is the general way, the ability to figure out how to accomplish it, a system of priorities, so that putting the two together you know how to react in any situation. Their first result is your ultimate goal for yourself, the *ratzon kadum*: the first thing your *reshimu* and *Kav* create.

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף הראשון שבו הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה,
שזהו כמשל רצון הכללי לבנין גדול כולל כל מה שבפרטיו מראשו לסופו בבת א'
ואחר כך מתחלק בו בסדר והדרגה מכלל לפרט
phrases.en: Then this gets split up,

phrases.he: על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like in the *mashal* we said about the house.

blocks.text: Its first *makif* is called *tehiru tata'a*, like the general will for a great building that includes all its details from beginning to end. In a person's whole life, this is like the general desire for fulfillment, or self-expression, or something like that. **Then this gets split up**: this is your top priority, your original goal.

This is like the *etzem* of the *yechida*, the *Moshiach* within each person. A person who finds it is redeemed: "they found the geula, they're fulfilled, they've arrived, whatever you want to call it." Then it splits into lesser priorities, a whole hierarchy according to your *Kav*, down to what you want in day-to-day life, **like in the mashal we said about the house.**

phrases.he: והיינו כמו כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט ההיולי לבא לגלוי דוקא, היה כולל כל פרטי הרצונות
phrases.en: And this is the *inyan* that when he had a particular *ratzon*, it came out, he already had all the things that he wants to do included in that.

phrases.he: והוא הרצון הכולל כולם,
phrases.en: and this first *ratzon* that comes out *b'gilui* includes them all,

phrases.he: ונקרא רצון קדום לכל מה שבא אחריו
phrases.en: This is called the original *ratzon* for everything that comes after.

blocks.text: When it rose in His simple will to come *davka* into revelation, it included all the particular wills: **when he had a particular ratzon, it came out, he already had all the things that he wants to do included in that**, **and this first ratzon that comes out b'gilui includes them all.** **This is called the original ratzon for everything that comes after**, the *ratzon kadum*: original, because everything else is only its details, a means to this goal.

That is the difference between *kadum* and *rishon*: *rishon* (first) just comes first, in any order; *kadum* means the things after it have no meaning but to fulfill it.

The will for money, for example, is not essential. It serves a deeper will: to buy what you need, to have possessions, which may mean doing what you want without worrying, or stature, people considering you successful. Trace all the wills back and you come to one essential desire, the inner goal.

sections.title: Down to the last detail, all included in the first circle around all four worlds
sections.summary: From the *ratzon kadum* come the particular wills: for *Atzilus* with its ten *sefiros*, still hidden until it is revealed, then to create *Beriya*, down to the last will of *Asiya*. All of them are included in the first circle, the beginning of the *Kav*, which surrounds the four worlds equally because they are all equally only a means to its goal. That they can be cut off from it is the root of *Tohu*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך בא רצון זה דרך פרט,
phrases.en: And then the details are revealed,

phrases.he: כמו הרצון להאציל
phrases.en: like the desire for *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: ובו כלול עשר ספירות בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: and this includes ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: ועדיין הכל בהעלם
phrases.en: but you didn't actually do *Atzilus* yet.

phrases.he: עד שבא לידי גלוי שהוא כשנאצל האור בבחינת האצילות כו'
phrases.en: then it comes *b'gilui*: that's when he actually was *ne'etzal*.

blocks.text: **And then the details are revealed, like the desire for Atzilus.** In the house *mashal* from before, the newly married man goes to the architect. The will for *Atzilus* is figuring out what you want: the architect asks, "What are you looking for?" and you are not talking about a house; "you're talking about yourself, what you like." **And this includes ten sefiros** with all their details.

blocks.title: Out to dinner, and the door
blocks.text: **But you didn't actually do Atzilus yet**: it is all hidden. As people say: "What are you going to do tonight?" "Let's go out for dinner." You drive there and get to the door: "Where are we going to get the *ratzon* to open the door?" "That was included in the *ratzon* to go to the restaurant." All the later wills you know will have to happen are included in the original desire.

blocks.title: Shall we drive to the real estate agent?
blocks.text: Like a guy who wants a house but has not thought of it yet: ask him, "Do you want a kitchen?" "Yeah, of course I want a kitchen." "So are we going to drive to the real estate agent?" "Oh yeah, sure." He did not think about the details, but it is understood that whatever has to be done for it, he wants to do.

So in *tehiru tata'a* they are included not in actuality but as one general thought, the first will that includes all the later ones. When they come up in actuality, those are the later circles, the *igulim* of *Atzilus* and of *Beriya*, where it splits up into each thing. To relate to a specific manifestation in a physical, limited world you have to pick a form, really a *kli*, and that is more like *tehiru tata'a*.

There is a *yechida* with a name and one without. The one with a name is the *ratzon kadum* of *Adam Kadmon*, its *igulim* and *yosher*: a picture of your essence. The real essence, the *yechida* without a name, *Yachid*, is like before the *tzimtzum*; included in it is that you can have *chesed*, like *Echad*, and *Malchus*, like *Kadmon*, which is why he highlights those two wills.

There is the ability to pick a general, abstract desire, transcending form, that includes everything; and the ability to pick a particular *kli* to express that transcendent thing, which is like *Kadmon*, or *Malchus*. In the *etzem* these two, like *chesed* and *gevura*, are only a *yecholes* (an ability), not divided out yet: the *etzem* is just the *etzem*, so it can do both. The *tzimtzum* is choosing which *Echad* and *Kadmon* you want, and its result is *tehiru tata'a*.

But you do not yet know it is a house, a building. You only know that you want to express a certain *inyan* of yourself, and you have to look for what will express it: wanting a *taanug* of feeling independent, you go looking and find the desire for a house to match.

That is the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, spoken of later, when you make your world view and self-image. When you normally say an *etzem*, or a person, you mean it already limited to being a person, with only ten *sefiros*; those limitations start in the *ratzon kadum* of *Adam Kadmon*. "Adam Kadmon is the first time it's like a person."

That came from the *tzimtzum*, and the chain in the person runs at the same time as the chain in the worlds: G-d's *ratzon kadum* made the soul of a certain form, and the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* made the way the soul goes into the body, its general mission.

The *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* is like *Moshiach*, the form of *Moshiach* as a person; the *igulim* of *Adam Kadmon* are like the *dira b'tachtonim*, its *pnimiyus*. The *nekuda*, the *ratzon kadum*, is the *dira b'tachtonim*; how it is expressed in our world is all that the *halacha* and *Midrashim* say about how it will physically be by *Moshiach*.

And after that, **then it comes b'gilui: that's when he actually was ne'etzal** (emanated). *Atzilus* is the revelation of the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* of *Atzilus* that were included in the original thing.

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון לברוא
phrases.en: the next *ratzon* is the *ratzon* to create,

phrases.he: יש מאין כו'
ובו שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and then it also has ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: עד הרצון היותר אחרון
phrases.en: so the final most *ratzon*,

phrases.he: שהוא כל אשר חפץ עשה כו', סוף הכל

blocks.text: Then it comes out in revelation: **the next ratzon is the ratzon to create**, figuring out what will fulfill your desires. A desire to swim, make a swimming pool; for *farbrengens*, a dining room with room and a floor that is not carpet, to clean up messes. That is *Beriya*: not the actual *Beriya* but the desire for it, its *igulim*. The will to create *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing), with *sechel* and *middos*: **and then it also has ten sefiros.**

Down to **the final most ratzon**, "all that He desired, He did": in the house, putting up the *mezuza*, moving in the furniture, the last fine touches; in the world, all the little details of everyday physical life, like the weather today. That is *Asiya* in action, the end of everything.

phrases.he: וכל פרטים הללו נכללו ברצון הקדום
phrases.en: all these details, they were all included in the original desire

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת השפעה על כל פנים אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: which is already an actual *hashpaa*, an actual thing that relates to the outside world, and after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ראשית הקו כו',
phrases.en: and this first circle is considered the beginning of the *Kav*, it's the first *gilui* of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: והיינו עיגול הראשון שאחר המשכת ראשית הקו ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: this is the first circle after the *hiyuli Kav*,

blocks.text: **All these details, they were all included in the original desire**, **which is already an actual hashpaa** (influence), **an actual thing that relates to the outside world, and after the tzimtzum.** **And this first circle is considered the beginning of the Kav, it's the first gilui of the Kav.** *Reshis hakav* can mean the *hiyuli Kav*, or this first circle, its first revelation: along the *Kav*, the top priority.

Practically, this is what it says in *HaYom Yom*: every single detail of creation, even the way a blade of grass sways in the wind, is not only by *hashgacha pratis* (individual Divine providence), but is necessary for the entire *kavana* (intent) of creation.

blocks.title: The leaves in this corner
blocks.text: When G-d said, "I want a *dira b'tachtonim*," you ask Him, "Well, do You want the leaves on the tree in this and this corner to blow back and forth 300,267,371 times?" And Hashem says, "Of course. How else could I have a *dira b'tachtonim* if it wasn't just like that?"

Every single *prat* is there for a reason we do not appreciate now but will throughout the seventh millennium. All the details of creation exist only as tools to fulfill this will, each fulfilling a certain detail of it, "or else they wouldn't exist." **This is the first circle after the hiyuli Kav.**

phrases.he: שנקרא מקיף כללי לכללות כל הד' עולמות דאבי''ע,
phrases.en: this first *ratzon* is called the general *makif* for all the four worlds of *ABYA*,

phrases.he: שמקיף אותם בשוה
phrases.en: that it surrounds them all equally, meaning that they're all equally just a means to accomplish this goal.

phrases.he: שנקרא מחשבה כללית שצופה ומביט בסקירה א' מראש לסוף הכל כו'
phrases.en: it's called a general thought that it sees everything in one glance.

blocks.text: **This first ratzon is called the general makif for all the four worlds of ABYA**, **that it surrounds them all equally, meaning that they're all equally just a means to accomplish this goal.** The *Kav* sets their order, but it need not be so: each will comes directly from the *ratzon hamuchlat*; the *Kav* just decides the priority. "That's why a person's ratzonos can jump out of place."

blocks.title: The son who forgot his mother
blocks.text: There are stories of someone from a very poor family whose dream was one day to support his poor mother and give her a better life. He goes to work, makes a lot of money, gets caught up in the desire for money and forgets his mother. He won't give her money; he might not even give to himself, he might become a miser. Or people who get all into business and forget their families, when the whole reason they worked was to have the means for what they really enjoy: *Torah* and *mitzvos*, their family, the people important to them.

How does a person forget? It is the thing of *Tohu*. Since each will has the *etzem* in it, you can get locked into it, feel the *taanug* and self-expression in it, and forget the need for anything else, without it being a means to an end. A means to an end is *tikun* (rectification). "But that's also part of the bechira."

That is why *Tohu* is so powerful: it takes a certain maturity to appreciate the deeper *taanug* in having it this way, with priorities. *Igulim* and *yosher* are the root of *Tohu* and *tikun*, to be spoken of later.

This first circle is called a general thought: **it's called a general thought that it sees everything in one glance.**

phrases.he: וזהו ביאור ענין כללי לכללות ענין הקו הזה
phrases.en: this is the general idea of the *Kav*,

phrases.he: ופרטי אופניו במה שמתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: and the details of how it circles and circles again,

phrases.he: יובן לפי אופן משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: now we can understand the general idea of what we mean by concentric circles by this *mashal*.

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בסמוך בעזרת ה׳ ודי למבין:
phrases.en: and now we'll explain more about it in the next chapter

blocks.text: **This is the general idea of the Kav**: it starts off as a general thing, then measures out the details. **And the details of how it circles and circles again**: **now we can understand the general idea of what we mean by concentric circles by this mashal.** **And now we'll explain more about it in the next chapter**: circle inside of circle, and how in *yosher* it is the opposite.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the *igulim* and the *yosher* of the *Kav*, and what do the water in the carved troughs and the soul before and in the body show about them?
Why is the first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, compared to a teacher's ultimate goal, and what does the story of Rabbi Chodakov and the *shliach* teach about it?
How is the *ratzon hamuchlat* like an artist's style, and why does it have no general and particular?
What makes a will *murkav*, and how does the will for a house show it?
Why is *tehiru tata'a* a lower purity than *tehiru ila'a*, though both are G-d's self-knowledge?
Why does the first circle surround the four worlds equally, and how can a person's wills "jump out of place"?

omitted.note: "Yeah, you can open it." Said to someone in the room.

notes.text: A listener is present in these tapes, unlike chapter 10: a student asks "A spring?" (49 w181-182), and he answers questions we do not hear ("I told you this story that he said there?" 49 w1143-1186; "This is the machshava kduma, yeah" 49 w1564-1570; "That's already muchlat, yeah. Murkav, right." 50 w1433-1438; "Yeah, you can open it" 50 w1849-1853). Only the spring question is audible enough for a question block.

The transcript hears "tehiru" as "tziyur" ("tziyur ila'a", "tziyur tata'a", 51 w658-720; "tziyur d'tata'a", 52 w329-717) and line 31's "tehiru tata'a" as "Toras Hashem" (51 w1877-1886). The blocks write tehiru ila'a and tehiru tata'a, as the chapter text has them.

Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: line 2, the end of line 4 and all of line 5, the start of line 7, the end of the first clause of line 8, "b'ofen kach v'kach" in line 18, line 24, the start of line 29 and all of line 30, lines 31 and 32, "yesh me'ayin" in line 38, and the end of line 39. Line 1's only English is his loose "Now we're going to explain the inyan of igulim v'yosher" (49 w67-76), kept for the whole line. Line 9's third phrase cites his rendering some sentences after its reading (49 w2295-2310, where he rereads it), and its last two phrases are in the next tape (50 w4-16, w76-86). Line 37's last phrase cites 52 w1118-1135, long after the line is first read, where he rereads it and says "that's when he actually was ne'etzal". Line 25's second phrase is only "like a taste" (51 w993-995); the sentence breaks off.

Rabbi Chodakov (the transcript's "Rabbi Chadkov") is presumably Rabbi Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov, the Rebbe's chief secretary; the story is told briefly and the shliach is not named. The story is left unflagged: it criticizes no one.

The block on Avraham and Yaakov (50 w2121-2208) is flagged "other" for "Yaakov having to lie and cheat Esav and Lavan": the teaching (they had to act against their nature) is kept, and the publishable text says "deal deceptively". He says he is not sure what it was by Yitzchak. A reviewer may decide this needs no flag. "The most liberal and the most conservative" of the Rebbe's conduct (50 w2277-2332) was judged not to need a flag: it takes no political side.

"Like it says in HaYom Yom, every single detail of creation, even the way a blade of grass swings in the wind ... is necessary for the entire kavana of the beriya" (52 w1492-1542) is reported as he gives it; the reference was not checked.

"Even though this connects to the hispashtus of the ratzon" (line 27): he goes on in Hebrew ("she'yihyeh achar kach"), so the English stops there. "V'ba'in zeh achar zeh b'hishtalshelus" (line 15) is one phrase, because "zeh" repeats; his English covers "one after the other" only.

Reviewer: line 34 is heard by the transcript as "birtzono hapashut d'yihyeh lo bayis lo l'gilui" (51 w2042-2057), a mishearing of "hahiyuli lavo l'gilui"; the block follows the chapter text and no longer speaks of "a house of his own". Line 9's first phrase now ends at "b'atzmo"; "eich la'asos davar chesed ploni" is read without an English of its own (his "how he'll want to do a particular chesed ploni" comes later, 49 w2120-2165, in the explanation). Line 22's "she'kolel hakol b'skira achas" is read without English. The "tribal chief in Africa" remark (50 w886-905) is now flagged other-groups; a human may judge it harmless.
